COMP 5222.title: Advanced Machine Learning with Graphs
COMP 5222.description: This course will introduce a number of advanced learning methods and modeling principles for analyzing large-scale complex data structures and graph data. Topics covered include semi-supervised learning, spectral graph theory, deep graph modeling, knowledge graph modeling, etc., as well as open research problems in this area.
cilos: Demonstrate machine learning algorithm design skills for graph data analytics tasks.
Analyze the quality of results to domain problems.
Develop a program that can handle existing real problems.

COMP 5311.title: Database Architecture and Implementation
COMP 5311.description: Introduction to the relational model and SQL.  System architectures and implementation techniques of database management systems: disk and memory management, access methods, implementation of relational operators, query processing and optimization, transaction management and recovery.  Hands on experience with building the components of a small DBMS.
cilos: Demonstrate a deep understanding of the field of data management. Learn concepts related to data base systems, applications and algorithms.
Learn current research trends in data management research and obtain the ability to produce novel research and engineering results.

Through presentations and literature surveys, the students will improve their communication skills. They are also expected to clearly interpret research or engineering concepts to specialist and general audiences.
The students will learn research topics and techniques  related to data management, which will enhance their ability as researchers in academia, or practitioners in industry.
Learn the principles of ethics, including appropriate citations of related work and repeatability of experiments.
Acquire sufficient knowledge of data management for undergraduate teaching and assessment of student learning.

COMP 5331.title: Knowledge Discovery in Databases
COMP 5331.description: An introduction to knowledge discovery in databases.  Different discovery and learning techniques are presented and compared.  Automatic generation of query language expressions is discussed in depth.  Potential applications are shown.
cilos: Describe basic concepts about data mining and knowledge discovery.
Apply clustering algorithms to cluster relational data.
Apply classification algorithms to relational data.
Use frequent pattern mining solutions to identify frequent patterns and association rules.
Apply outlier detection methods to detect outliers.

COMP 5411.title: Advanced Computer Graphics
COMP 5411.description: The first part of this course covers an introduction to mathematical tools and computational techniques for image synthesis and manipulation of 3D models.  The second part covers more advanced topics which may include digital geometry processing, image processing, visualization, GPU computing, numerical optimization methods.
cilos: Understanding of algorithms and mathematics for representing, manipulating and analyzing geometric data.
Understanding how the GPU's rendering pipeline operates.
Understanding of algorithms and mathematics for advanced real-time rendering.
Ability to explain principles and different techniques used for real-time rendering and understand their trade-offs.
Ability to design and implement graphics applications for geometry processing and real-time rendering.

COMP 5421.title: Computer Vision
COMP 5421.description: Introduction to techniques for automatically describing visual data and tools for image analysis; perception of spatial organization; models of general purpose vision systems; computational and psychological models of perception.
cilos: Implement practical various AI solutions by applying relevant computer vision algorithms.
Demonstrate capability of visual recognition to robotics and intelligent systems.
Identify key problems in contemporary computer visionfor further research.
Develop practical computer vision systems for various recognition tasks such as autonomous driving and video surveillance.

COMP 5422.title: Deep 2D and 3D Visual Scene Understanding
COMP 5422.description: Visual scene understanding is an important and fundamental field for advanced application scenarios such as self-driving, robotics, and AR/VR. This course majorly focuses on delivering deep learning-based visual scene understanding techniques in both 2D and 3D perspectives. In the 2D part, it introduces topics including image and scene classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection/tracking. In the 3D part, it delivers how 3D scene understanding can be performed through learning from 2D images, point clouds or multi-modal data, involving topics such as scene depth estimation, camera pose prediction, 3D scene reconstruction, and visual SLAM. Representative deep scene understanding architectures and frameworks in supervised, self-supervised, and open-world learning settings will also be introduced.
cilos: Learn fundamentals in deep learning-based architectures/frameworks for various important 2D and 3D visual scene understanding tasks.
Obtain knowledge of visual scene understanding techniques for various intelligent applications in selfdriving, robotics, and AR/VR.
Gain a sense of current research and development trends in academia and industry in the domain of visual scene understanding.
Learn state-of-the-art results in visual scene understanding, and develop research and implementation skills.
Learn to transfer knowledge and skills from deep visual scene understanding to design and develop novel applications in other related AI domains.

COMP 5423.title: Deep Learning for Medical Image Analysis
COMP 5423.description: Nowadays medical image analysis is rapidly growing and plays an indispensable role in healthcare. Recent advances of deep learning techniques have made significant breakthroughs in medical image analysis applications. This course will cover fundamental knowledge of medical imaging and various medical image analysis tasks, including computer-aided detection, segmentation, diagnosis and prognosis. Deep learning methods for solving these tasks will be introduced and state-of-the-art methods will be discussed. The remaining significant challenges and limitations will also be presented, including limited amount of labeled data, deep learning with interpretation and generalization issues, etc. This course will equip students with practical knowledge of medical imaging and analysis with deep learning techniques.
cilos: Explain the different medical imaging techniques and various medical image analysis tasks.
Obtain the fundamentals in deep learning methods with application to medical imaging and analysis.
Explain and apply the skills of deep learning technologies in medical image analysis tasks, including computer-aided detection, diagnosis and prognosis, etc.
Identify and explain the state-of-the-art deep learning approaches for medical imaging applications.
Gain the current research and development trends in both academia and industry in the domain of medical imaging and analysis.

COMP 5424.title: Deep Multimodal Understanding and Generation
COMP 5424.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to recent advances in multimodal machine learning, with a focus on vision-language research. Major topics include multimodal understanding (including translation, multimodal reasoning, multimodal alignment, multimodal information extraction), multimodal generation, multimodal pretraining and adaptation, and recent techniques and trends in multimodal research. The course structure will primarily consist of instructor presentation, assignment, and final project report.
cilos: Understand mainstream multimodal topics and tasks.
Learn deep architectures for multimodal learning.
Know how to utilize recent machine learning techniques in multimodal research.
Apply critical thinking and problem solving skills, such as identifying and explaining the state-of-the-art approaches for multimodal applications.
Gain the current research and development trends in both academia and industry in the domain of multimodal learning.

COMP 5551.title: Advanced Large-Scale Machine Learning Systems for Foundation Models
COMP 5551.description: In recent years, foundation models have fundamentally revolutionized the state-of-the-art of artificial intelligence. This course unravels the secrets of the efficient deployment of such workflows from the system perspective. Specifically, it will explain how a modern machine learning system (i.e., PyTorch) works and discuss main distributed infrastructure for foundation model training and inference deployment.
cilos: Understand core concepts and principles in foundation models.
Understand core concepts in large-scale distributed machine learning systems.
Master the core principles in design and implement new system optimizations for AI workflows.
Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills, such as identifying and explaining the state-of-the-art approaches for foundation model  applications.
Gain the current research and development trends in both academia and industry in the domain of machine learning systems.

COMP 5621.title: Computer Networks
COMP 5621.description: Principles, design and implementation of computer communication networks; network architecture and protocols, OSI reference model and TCP/IP networking architecture; Internet applications and requirements; transport protocols, TCP and UDP; network layer protocols, IP, routing, multicasting and broadcasting; local area networks; data link and physical layer issues; TCP congestion control, quality of service, emerging trends in networking.
cilos: Understand and explain data communications networks, their components, the technologies behind them, the network organization.
Identify and classify the different functionalities necessary for building viable communication networks, and be able.
Explain the TCP/IP protocol family and how each of the TCP, UDP and IP protocols contribute to implementing the Internet.
Understand the difference between different switching techniques (packet switching vs. Circuit switching).
Understand the factors that impact network performance and how to strike a balance between complexity and performance.
Understand the basic principles behind network applications.
Understand the principles behind transport layer protocols, the services they provide, and build an understanding of basic.
Explain the differences between routing and forwarding and how a router functions.
Show an understanding of intra-domain and inter-domain routing and how these are instantiated in the Internet through protocols.
Show an understanding of the principles behind the link layer, its instantiation and implementation in various networking technologies.

COMP 5631.title: Cryptography and Security
COMP 5631.description: Classical encryption techniques, block and stream ciphers, public-key cryptography, authentication, nonrepudiation, key management, digital signatures, public key infrastructure, cryptographic protocol, secret sharing, electronic mail security, IP security, Web security, Firewalls, Intrusion detection.
cilos: Demonstrate a systematic understanding of cryptography and security.
Get familiar with real-world security systems, and be able to handle real-world security events.
Establish the theory foundation for doing research in security-related topics.
Improve communication capability in writing and oral presentations.

COMP 5711.title: Introduction to Advanced Algorithmic Techniques
COMP 5711.description: This is an introductory graduate course in algorithmic techniques.  Topics include: advanced data structures; graph algorithms; amortization; approximation algorithms; on-line algorithms; randomized and probabilistic analysis.
cilos: Demonstrate an understanding of the theory of advanced algorithm design and analysis techniques.
Demonstrate an ability to design algorithms using techniques such as randomization, hashing, and online algorithms.
Demonstrate an ability to analyze algorithms using parameterization, amortization, and approximation.

COMP 5712.title: Introduction to Combinatorial Optimization
COMP 5712.description: An introduction to the basic tools of combinatorial optimization, including network flow and the max-flow min-cut theorem, linear programming, matching, spanning trees and matroids, dynamic programming, algorithms and data structures, graph algorithms.
cilos: Demonstrate an understanding of the mathematical theory underlying algorithms for combinatorial optimization.
Demonstrate an ability to use linear and integer programming to formulate different combinatorial problems.
Demonstrate an ability to apply various techniques to design approximation algorithms for hard problems.

COMP 5713.title: Computational Geometry
COMP 5713.description: An introductory course in Computational Geometry.  Algorithms for manipulating geometric objects.  Topics include Convex Hulls, Voronoi Diagrams, Point Location, Triangulations, Randomized Algorithms, Point-Line Duality.
cilos: Demonstrate ability to solve basic problems in computational geometry.
Understand some fundamental algorithmic techniques in computational geometry.
Demonstrate ability to design and analyse algorithms using the fundamental techniques in computational geometry.

COMP 5911.title: Entrepreneurial Me
COMP 5911.description: While entrepreneurship is a career choice, its mindset is for everyone. This is a course covering the mindset and elements of founding new and innovative business ventures in information technology sector. Topics include the entrepreneurial risk-taking value-creation mindset, market identification and go-to-market strategies, business models and development, business plan, fundraising and investment, role and protection of intellectual properties, technology-market gap and product-market fit, and growth and exit strategies. Case studies of successful and unsuccessful ventures will be discussed. In-class student participation and presentation are expected. Business and non-engineering students interested in starting IT-related companies are also welcome. Research postgraduate students are encouraged to develop proof-of-concept prototypes and business plans based on their research findings.
cilos: Identify the basic principles and practices involved in either starting a company or planning to work in a start-up company, and any pitfalls to be avoided.
Summarize the basic principles of IT entrepreneurship.
Recognize and act upon opportunities for building a personal business network.
Evaluate potential business opportunities and develop appropriate decision-making skills so as to take best advantage of those opportunities.
Understand and communicate the business potential of one’s research project or a deep technology.

cilos: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of selected topics in software engineering of current interest to the Department and not covered by existing courses.

COMP 6211.description: Advanced topics in artificial intelligence including neural networks, natural language processing, logic programming, image understanding, robotics and others.

COMP 6511.title: Topics in Computer Systems Analysis
COMP 6511.description: Advanced topics in computer systems analysis; issues in the development and solution of system models; model parametrization, verification and validation; recent developments in techniques and tools for system evaluation.
cilos: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of advanced topics in computer systems analysis; issues in the development and solution of system models; model parametrization, verification and validation; recent developments in techniques and tools for system evaluation.

COMP 6611.title: Topics in Computer and Communication Networks
COMP 6611.description: Advanced topics in communication networks, including issues in high speed networking, ATM, multimedia communication, network interconnection, network management, and protocol verification and testing.
cilos: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of advanced topics in communication networks, including issues in high speed networking, ATM, multimedia communication, network interconnection, network management, and protocol verification and testing.

COMP 6612.description: Selected topics in computer engineering of current interest to the Department and not covered by existing courses.
cilos: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of selected topics in computer engineering of current interest to the Department and not covered by existing courses.

COMP 6613.title: Topics in Applications of Computer Science and Engineering
COMP 6613.description: Selected topics in applications of computer science not covered by existing course.  Credits earned by taking this course can only be used to satisfy the breath requirement of the research area of Software and Applications.

COMP 6711.title: Topics in Theoretical Computer Science
COMP 6711.description: Selected topics in theoretical computer science not covered by existing courses, including, but not limited to, computational complexities and computability, graph algorithms and combinatorial optimization.

COMP 6911.title: Computer Science and Engineering Seminar I

Make a contribution to their specific field of study through either original research or substantial engineering efforts.

COMP 7990.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
